weighted_score_formula: score = corr * corr_multiplier + mmc * mmc_multiplier; payout = stake * clip(payout_factor * score, -0.05, +0.05); payout_factor = min(1, stake_threshold / total_at_risk)

bmc.detail: v5.3 validation_benchmark_models.parquet publishes exactly two single-model benchmark columns (v53_lgbm_ender20, v53_lgbm_ender60). No official historical Benchmark Meta Model aggregate column and no historical benchmark stake weights are published, so official BMC cannot be reproduced from published files. A single benchmark or an equal-weight average is NOT the BMM and is not reported as BMC.

target_authority_resolution.evidence: Cyrus was the payout target from 2023 until 2025-12-31 and was replaced by Ender-20 effective 2026-01-01 (first payout-target change since 2023). The v5.3 Quantum release (2026-07-15) states the payout target is remaining the same. v5.3 files contain no plain cyrus target column (only auxiliary target_cyrusd_20/60); target_ender_20 is present and resolves on the 20D2L cadence. MR28's assertion was therefore correct; the target_cyrus_20 expectation was stale.
target_authority_resolution.bare_target_alias: In v5.3 the bare `target` column is byte-identical to target_ender_60 on pre-holdout eras (NaN pattern included) and is a dataset default, not the payout authority. The harness rejects `target` as a payout-target configuration.

pending_transition.name: Ender-60 scoring cutover
pending_transition.detail: Current scoring docs state that starting with a separately coordinated cutover round, CORR and MMC will use the 60-day Ender target (CORR60/MMC60). As of retrieval, payouts remain on the 20-day Ender target. When the cutover round is announced and effected, this record is stale and must be re-issued.

revalidation: These values change over time (multipliers changed 2026-01-01; the payout target changed 2026-01-01; an Ender-60 cutover is announced). This record must be re-audited against live documentation, round configuration, and current dataset files before any deployment, staking, or payout-relevant use. It may not be assumed current.
